findings.title: The rules enforce a private copy of MODULES; test/arch/modules.ts is not read by any rule
findings.detail: rules.ts defines and exports its own `MODULES` literal and uses it as the default for checkGraphIntegrity, checkModuleGraph, checkNetwork and checkAll. test/arch/modules.ts holds a second, independent literal; it is not a re-export, despite the implementer's note. The design says a later unit adds a module or edge by editing test/arch/modules.ts in its red step, and every ARCH_MODULE_EDGE message points to that file. Such an edit would change nothing the rules enforce, and the two copies can drift silently. This was done to work around F-35492b20 (the base replay removes modules.ts).
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the graph data in one place, with modules.ts as the single source. Make the rules import it, or have rules.ts read it so the harness replay still works, and add a test that asserts the two are the same object.

findings.title: A default import beside all-`type` named specifiers is classed as type-only, which bypasses the network and console rules
findings.detail: namedBindingsAreTypeOnly ignores the default binding of the import clause. For `import https, { type Agent } from "node:https";` it returns true, so checkNetwork skips the value import `https` in any module (and checkConsole skips the same form for node:console). Design decision 3 makes only declarations with *only* named, all-type specifiers type-only.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN `src/api/a.ts` has `import https, { type Agent } from "node:https";` THEN collectImports returns it with typeOnly true and checkNetwork returns [].

findings.title: The secret scan silently excludes every path under a `.l4` directory
findings.detail: listScannableFiles drops any path with a `.l4` component. The requirement is to scan every tracked and untracked-not-ignored file outside seed/. The implementer added this exclusion to clear a real-tree violation in harness evidence (.l4/evidence/round-2/verdict.json). Tree-blockers requirement C-eea53b80 says to raise a blocker instead of narrowing a rule. A secret pasted under any `.l4/` path is now never reported.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a tracked or untracked file lies under a `.l4` directory at any depth THEN listScannableFiles omits it and scanRepository reports no ARCH_SECRET for it.

Design decision 3 makes a declaration type-only only when it has nothing but named specifiers, at least one, all `type`-modified. This bypasses the network and worker_threads rules. findings.title: The rules enforce a private copy of MODULES; test/arch/modules.ts is not read by any rule
findings.detail: rules.ts defines and exports its own `MODULES` literal and uses it as the default for checkGraphIntegrity, checkModuleGraph, checkNetwork and checkAll. test/arch/modules.ts holds a second, independent literal; it is not a re-export, despite the implementer's note. The design says a later unit adds a module or edge by editing test/arch/modules.ts in its red step, and every ARCH_MODULE_EDGE message points to that file. Such an edit would change nothing the rules enforce, and the two copies can drift silently. This was done to work around F-35492b20 (the base replay removes modules.ts).

Design decision 3 makes only declarations with *only* named, all-type specifiers type-only.
